1.hint: Connect to your lab server over SSH as ec2-user.

4.hint: sudo dnf list installed | grep -i postgres - confirm nothing is installed yet.

5.hint: Install the PGDG repo RPM (the `sudo dnf install ... pgdg-redhat-repo-latest.noarch.rpm` command).

6.hint: sudo dnf -qy module disable postgresql - disable the built-in module.

7.hint: Install the packages: `sudo dnf install -y postgresql16 postgresql16-server postgresql16-contrib postgresql16-libs`.

8.hint: sudo dnf list installed | grep postgresql16 - confirm the 4 packages.

9.hint: id postgres - the postgres OS user exists.

12.done: your data directory at /opt/pgsql/data is initialized

13.hint: sudo ls /opt/pgsql/data/ - see the initialized cluster files.

16.hint: cat the override file - confirm its two lines.

17.hint: Reload systemd so it reads your override: `sudo systemctl daemon-reload`.
17.done: systemd has loaded your PGDATA override

18.hint: Start it: `sudo systemctl daemon-reload` then `sudo systemctl start postgresql-16`.

19.hint: sudo systemctl status postgresql-16 - confirm active (running).

20.hint: Enable it at boot: `sudo systemctl enable postgresql-16`.
20.done: PostgreSQL 16 will start automatically on boot

21.hint: sudo su - postgres - become the database superuser.

23.hint: SELECT version(); - confirm the server responds.
